name: @subline/installer

scripts.//pack: Packaging is a CONFIG step, not a rewrite: build:mod produces build/mod, build:app produces dist, and electron-builder copies both.
scripts.//dist:win: Unsigned, deliberately — spec §1 and §10. See docs/RELEASING.md for what SmartScreen does about it.
scripts.//release: Clean checkout → signed, notarized, stapled artefacts + the release manifest. One command. Needs the credentials named in docs/RELEASING.md.

//engines: buildMod.mjs imports src/bundle/spec.ts directly, so that the checks the build runs and the checks the installer runs are the same code. packaging/hooks.mjs does the same. Node strips TypeScript types without a flag from 22.18 on.

directories.//buildResources: NOT the default `build/`, which is the gitignored home of the assembled mod bundle and the pinned Vencord checkout. `packaging/` holds the entitlements and the hooks, which are inputs.

build.//extraResources: The mod bundle ships in Contents/Resources/mod and is COPIED OUT to ~/Library/Application Support/Subline/mod on install. It must never be loaded from here: see src/app/modInstall.ts — App Translocation would make the path vanish and stop Discord starting.
build.//hooks: packaging/hooks.mjs exports one function per hook name. beforePack and afterPack refuse to ship a mod bundle whose build id disagrees with the plugin stamp in this checkout; afterSign notarizes and staples. A configuration that quietly did not happen is this project's oldest failure mode.

mac.//identity: Deliberately unset. electron-builder auto-discovers the Developer ID Application certificate in the login keychain, or takes CSC_LINK + CSC_KEY_PASSWORD from the environment. Pinning a name here would put a Team ID in the repository and break every other machine.
mac.//entitlements: Read packaging/entitlements.mac.plist before changing this. In particular: NO entitlement grants the right to modify another application. That is TCC's App Management, a user grant in System Settings, and it attaches to the SIGNING IDENTITY — which is why spec §4 requires Developer ID and why the app is not sandboxed.
mac.//notarize: false because packaging/hooks.mjs afterSign runs notarytool itself and staples the .app before the DMG wraps it — electron-builder's own step would not staple the app, only the archive.

extendInfo.//NSAppleEventsUsageDescription: The string macOS shows in the Automation prompt when Subline asks Discord to quit (spec §7: offer, never force-kill). Unlike App Management's wording, this one is ours to write.
extendInfo.NSAppleEventsUsageDescription: Subline asks Discord to quit before it changes it, so nothing you are part-way through typing is lost.

dmg.//: Not signed: the app inside it is signed, notarized and stapled, which is what Gatekeeper checks. The release script notarizes and staples the DMG itself afterwards.

win.//signing: UNSIGNED, deliberately — spec §1 and §10: an EV certificate needs a registered business and ~$500/yr, which is not justifiable pre-revenue. See docs/RELEASING.md for what users will see and for the ONE result that changes this decision (Defender quarantine, not the SmartScreen warning).
win.//adding-a-certificate: A config change, not a rewrite: set CSC_LINK (path or base64 of the .pfx) and CSC_KEY_PASSWORD in the environment and electron-builder signs with no edit here at all. For a hardware token, add `certificateSubjectName` and `signingHashAlgorithms` to this block.

nsis.//perMachine: Spec §5: Discord lives in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Discord, per-user, so there is no UAC gate and no reason to ask for one. An unsigned installer that also demands elevation is close to a textbook Defender heuristic (§10).
